new_hazards_found.summary: an in_source lexicon anchor can resolve to an OCCURRENCE (a footnote fragment, or a sentence saying where the word's referent is printed) rather than a definition; R37 proved the entry existed but never asked whether it defined anything

a page-FRACTION grow applied to a measured crop box swallows the neighbouring heading, and the no-clip assertion then reports the heading being clipped — sending you to widen a box that was already correct. Grow in PIXELS, and mask on the object's own ink colour rather than all ink.
new_hazards_found.why: the no-clip assertion already fires; what is left is a crop-authoring judgement (which ink belongs to the object) that varies per source and per plate. Encoded in the comments of work/arabic/u2/make_form_crops.py and in this manifest, not as a check.

new_hazards_found.summary: a crop taken from a duplex scan carries the reverse side's bleed-through, which Parker's figure bar forbids outright ('page-text bleed never ships'); every storage check was green and only the contact-sheet LOOK caught it
new_hazards_found.why: detecting it requires knowing which ink belongs to the plate — trivial here (the Writing rows are pure red) but not general. The mandatory contact-sheet review is the guard; the fix (compositing the target ink over flat paper) is in make_form_crops.redonly().
